https://www.thetimes.com/uk/photography-.title: News in pictures: Tuesday June 4, 2024
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/photography-.text: For more pictures from The Times follow us on Instagram

image.caption: A patient lioness puts up with the antics of this cub, seen biting its mother’s tail at the Ngorongoro conservation area, Tanzania
The AeroSuperBatics wingwalkers perform at the Midlands Air Festival at Ragley Hall, Alcester, Warwickshire. The event’s sixth year included displays of night-time flying and hot-air balloons
Shadows lengthen as tourists ride camels in the Kubuqi Desert in Ordos, Inner Mongolia, northern China

Wounded Soul: Journey of Destruction, a bronze sculpture by Dia al-Azzawi, an Iranian artist, is expected to fetch up to £25,000 at an auction of  modern and contemporary Middle Eastern art at Bonhams, London, on June 5
Light from the evening sun shines on this Douglas pedigree Highland cow in a buttercup meadow at the Hirsel Estate, Coldstream

Militants from Extinction Rebellion and Stop Gravel walk on railway tracks at a gravel pit in Le Vernet, southwest France. They claim the site’s operation harms the environment. The protesters forced the gates of the site and damaged buildings and vehicles

The core of the Milky Way seen over Stonehenge, Wiltshire, on Friday. The image consists of 16 two-minute exposures using a motorised star tracker, and one two-minute exposure of the foreground, merged to reveal more detail than the naked eye can see

A puffin soaks in the early sunshine at Bempton Cliffs, Bridlington. The birds have returned to the colony after up to eight months wintering at sea as individuals, mainly in the Atlantic Ocean and North Sea, although some make it to the Mediterranean
Lizzo attends the WeHo Pride Parade in Los Angeles, California. The singer has a strong LGBT following and calls her fans Lizzbians
The crescent moon rises behind the Galata Tower in Istanbul, Turkey. The building, originally part of the city walls, dates to the 1200s

Manuel Lettenbichler performs in the Red Bull Erzberg Rodeo in Eisenerz, Austria. The 26-year-old Bavarian began riding at the age of five when his father bought him his first motorbike. At 16 he became the youngest rider to finish the world-renowned Erzberg Rodeo

Support dogs are greeted by athletes during the US gymnastics championships in Fort Worth, Texas. The event was won by Simone Biles, the four-times Olympic gold medallist, who will soon take to the apparatus in Paris

Survivors from the landslide in Papua New Guinea on May 24 prepare to be addressed by James Marape, the country’s prime minister. They have smeared themselves in mud as a sign of mourning. Hundreds of villagers are thought to have died in the disaster

This Qajar tile, made in Persia in the late 19th century, shows a ruler and his courtiers feasting in a palace. Similar examples can be found in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London. The item has an estimate of £700 to £900 and is due to be sold by Olympia Auctions tomorrow

Sculptures commissioned for Canterbury Cathedral will be installed and blessed on Saturday. Four angels that hold the scripture to the Sanctus, a songful prayer, were damaged during the Reformation. They are to be replaced with carvings by Nina Bilbey, whose studio is on the Holkham estate, Norfolk. Each of the 1,000-year-old originals was laser scanned and this showed they had different faces, probably based on someone known to the craftsman
Zhanna, a 16-year-old tigress, receives her annual check-up at Buffalo Zoo, New York state. The vets were happy with her health and Zhanna was soon back in her enclosure
A Palestinian man looks for useful items on a rubbish dump next to the Bureij refugeee camp in central Gaza, which was established in 1949. More than 28,000 people lived in the camp in 2017

Sprout, a swamp wallaby, had a rough start to life but is in safe hands now. The joey’s mother was hit by a car and killed but Sprout was thrown clear of her pouch. He is being treated at Byron Bay Wildlife Hospital, New South Wales, which is at risk of closure after a 70 per cent increase in patients drove up costs

People watch the official announcement of the South African general election results in Midrand, Johannesburg. The African National Congress lost its 30-year-old outright majority, winning only 159 seats in the 400-seat parliament
Yemeni honour guards carry the coffins of people killed in strikes by US and British forces. The allied action prompted Yemen’s Houthis to retaliate by launching drones and missiles

A cowboy takes a tumble in a bull-riding event in Brooklin, Ontario. The Ram Rodeo was part of the rural community’s spring fair, which also included bareback and saddlebronc riding, barrel racing and pole bending

A carriage and four horses arrive at Kiplin Hall, North Yorkshire, during filming of a documentary about George Calvert, the hall’s first owner and the founder of the US state of Maryland. The PBS documentary will mark the 400th anniversary of the hall next year and America’s 250th anniversary of independence in 2026

https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/articl.title: Barclays branches attacked by pro-Palestinian and climate activists
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/articl.subtitle: Premises across the country targeted over bank’s links to defence industry and fossil fuels
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/articl.text:
Branches of Barclays Bank up and down the country have had windows smashed and façades doused in red paint by pro-Palestinian protesters.
In an escalation of protests against the bank, Palestine Action and a climate change protest group called Shut the System targeted 15 branches in Manchester, Bristol, Glasgow, Brighton and London in the early hours of Monday.
Palestine Action said it attacked banks to demand it “divests from Israel’s weapons trade and fossil fuels”.
“Barclays is funding the crises of climate collapse and genocide in Palestine,” a spokeswoman for Palestine Action said. “Decades of polite campaigning, petitions, letter writing and lobbying MPs have failed.”
The group said it would continue to escalate protests “until Barclays pulls its finger out and stops funding genocide and climate destruction”.
Three men were arrested in connection with criminal damage at a Barclays branch in Moorgate, in the City of London.
At 3am the men, aged between 34 and 45, were caught on camera spraying the front of the building with red paint using an adapted fire extinguisher, according to a City of London police statement.
They ran away but were caught by police. “Our extensive camera network located the suspects and enabled our officers to swiftly get to the scene and effect arrests,” Detective Chief Inspector Andrew Spooner said. “Criminal damage of businesses and institutions will not be tolerated and will result in police action.”
In St John’s Wood, north London, the glass door to the branch was shattered and red paint was sprayed across the entrance and cash machines, mirroring a similar protest that took place last month.
In Edinburgh, stones inscribed with the names of Palestinians who have died during the war in Gaza were thrown through branch windows.
At another branch, activists sprayed the names of Palestinians killed in Israeli military action on the walls.
“We provide vital financial services to US, UK and European public companies that supply defence products to Nato and its allies,” a spokeswoman for Barclays said.
“Barclays does not directly invest in these companies. The defence sector is fundamental to our national security and the UK government has been clear that supporting defence companies is compatible with environmental, social and governance considerations. Decisions on the implementation of arms embargoes to other nations are the job of respective elected governments.“While we support the right to protest, we ask that campaigners do so in a way which respects our customers, colleagues and property.”
• How anti-Israel boycotts have hurt the high street
The Barclays branch in the Broadmead shopping quarter, Bristol, was sprayed and all its windows smashed. A spokesman for Avon and Somerset police said: “Investigating officers are keen to speak to anyone who saw three people wearing balaclavas leave Broadmead on bicycles shortly after the damage was caused.”
Greater Manchester police said: “We are investigating two reports of criminal damage from the early hours this morning [Monday, 10 June] involving red graffiti over buildings on Central Street, Bury, and Bridge Street, Stockport.
“To date, we have made 14 arrests in relation to 17 similar reports of criminal damage since October 2023 where buildings have been targeted with red paint across Greater Manchester. This behaviour is totally unacceptable and won’t be tolerated.”
Sussex police confirmed that they were also investigating.
Barclays is facing protests on other fronts, with several musicians pulling out of the Latitude music festival over Barclays’ sponsorship of the event. This followed more than 100 performers boycotting The Great Escape festival in Brighton last month, which was also sponsored by the bank.

In Moorgate ATMs were plugged with expanding foam
A cash machine in Peckham, southeast London, was also attacked by supporters of Palestine Action
Supporters of Palestine Action threw stones inscribed with the names of dead Palestinians and other slogans at Barclays in Edinburgh

https://www.thetimes.com/uk/photography-.title: Faces of joy and despair in Portrait of Humanity award shortlist
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/photography-.text:
The British Journal of Photography has announced the shortlist for its Portrait of Humanity prize, showcasing the diversity of human experiences across the world. Organisers say the collection of 200 images seeks to celebrate what unites us at times of division.
The 30 single-image winners and the three winning photo series will be revealed on Thursday. Winning artists will have their work displayed in a touring exhibition at Fotofestiwal in Lodz, Poland, the Four Corners gallery in London and the Indian Photo Festival in Hyderabad. All 200 shortlisted images feature in a book, Portrait of Humanity Volume 6, published in September by Bluecoat Press.

image.caption: In Akrê, Kurdish Iraq, fires are lit and thousands of people climb mountains with flaming torches to celebrate Newroz, the Kurdish New Year, which coincides with the spring equinox

Ganiyat and Maryam, sisters who live in Kaduna, Nigeria. The photographer says this portrait is intended to celebrate not only their deep bond but also the richness of diversity within their relationship
Skateboarding girls pictured in Mazar-e-Sharif, Afghanistan, part of a series on a local youth project called Skateistan
Russ Rowland follows a long tradition of street photographers who have found subjects among the crowds on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan
Mady and Monette Malroux, identical twins who have lived together their whole lives and often dress alike, have provided rich subject matter for a number of photographers
Sam Wright spent two years immersed in the Traveller community and hopes to challenge harmful stereotypes. This family was photographed at the Appleby horse fair in Cumbria
Nailan, eight, is one of the impoverished children who train at a community boxing gym in Cienfuegos, Cuba, with a punchbag slung from a tree and a training ring on a beach below the promenade

Anumukherjee, from Delhi, had acid thrown on her by a friend who was said to be jealous of her beauty. She had 22 operations but lost both eyes. The portrait is part of a long-term project about acid attack survivors around the world
A resident of the Kherson region of Ukraine dries the contents of her home after the Nova Kakhovka dam was destroyed in June last year, flooding towns and villages downstream
Giggling schoolgirls and sleepy boys on a boat trip in Hydra, Greece
Project Hope, a charitable outreach programme, uses play as a form of therapy for children growing up in a gang-blighted area of Cape Town where crossfire is a weekly occurrence
Baba Desi, 94, known as the Belgrave Wizard, is a spiritual healer, social campaigner and colourful local figure in an outer suburb of Melbourne

Teva Cosic and her mother live on the other side of the world from family in Sweden, but they try to keep a traditional Christmas by cooking Swedish food and dancing around a tree in the heat of Cairns, Australia

Ellie-Bea Thomas is a Special Olympics Team GB athlete who won two gold medals at the World Games in Berlin last year, competing in rhythmic gymnastics. The photographer is a great-great-grandson of John Langdon Down, who identified Down’s syndrome. “He believed in the values of creativity, performance and art in the support of people with learning disabilities, which are values Ellie-Bea embodies in every aspect of her life,” he says
Opal Onyx says that growing up on Jersey “made me buck against normality and the cult of conformity”. Now living in Melbourne, Onyx is a puppetmaker and theatre performer

The photographer spotted this well-dressed pair in a village on the outskirts if the Makgadikgadi salt pan in Botswana. “They knew each other but were not a couple, which seemed a pity given their collective style,” she says

“They Are Not Afraid of Riding Stallions” is a long-running series following a young man named Achraf with his friends and their horses in Diabat, near Essaouira, Morocco. The images explore friendship and manhood, reflecting on the intricate beauty of this transitional time when teenage years are left behind, the photographer says. Pictured is one of Achraf’s friends
An activist drums up support on Westminster Bridge in London, part of a publicity launch for Extinction Rebellion’s 100 Days campaign last year

Wan Rui fell in love with the Lolita fashion subculture almost ten years ago and is now a Lolita model, sharing images of herself on social media. The portrait is from a series on the Lolita community in China
Two women look out over the sea in Nice, France, in this image by the Swedish photographer Martina Holmberg
Anya Tsaruk documents her family and friends’ lives in Ukraine, challenging their portrayal mainly as victims of Russia’s war

author: The Times
